messages:
emma: heads up — noticed a jump in Loki p95 and a cluster of logs with empty trace ids around 02:06 UTC in us-central1. GPUs reporting trace_id="". anyone else seeing missing trace ids?
sre-oncall: alerts fired at 02:07: LokiQueryLatencyP95 and loki_ingester_write_errors. prom: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(loki_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) jumped from ~350ms to ~2.2s
loki-bot: Alert: [Loki] High query latency — labels: region=us-central1 app=gpu-ingest
jasper: checking node logs — lots of TCP resets to our kvcache/redis endpoints: `dial tcp 10.12.34.56:6379: connect: connection reset by peer` between 02:04-02:08. kube-proxy conntrack counters spiked on gpu nodes.
kube-admin: kube-proxy OOMKilled on 3 nodes at 02:04; conntrack table hit limit. sample from kube-proxy log: `W0502 02:04:12.123 conntrack.go:200] conntrack table full, dropping conn`
net-eng: we rotated managed NAT gateways in us-central1 at 02:03 for a security patch — expected some egress churn but didn't expect this level of drop.
emma: timeline matches. hypothesis: agents streaming logs retried over new sockets after resets and serializer dropped trace headers on requeue, so Loki got entries without @trace.id.
jasper: agent logs show `trace_id="" error=failed-write-retry` and `requeue: true` for batches that hit a socket reset. reproducer attached to INC.
marta: opening INC-3421, adding runbook link: https://wiki/internal/runbooks/conntrack-nat. tagging apps/infra.
sre-oncall: short-term mitigation: 1) bump conntrack max on gpu nodes: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` 2) widen local port range: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"` 3) add Prom rule for missing_trace_id_ratio > 1% over 5m
kube-admin: applied conntrack bump to two nodes, will roll to remainder. also setting `--conntrack-max-per-core=32768` on kube-proxy DaemonSet and scheduling rolling restarts.
net-eng: rolled NAT rollback for ~12 minutes while we triage. will reschedule patch with drained nodes and staged rollout. provider will also check ephemeral port reuse settings.
emma: can someone run a narrow Loki query to enumerate affected services? suggested LogQL: `{cluster="us-central1", job="kubernetes/containers"} |= "trace_id" | json | line_format "{container_name} {trace_id} {msg}"` and a Kibana query for ES: `NOT exists:@trace.id AND kubernetes.cluster.name: "us-central1"`
jasper: ran LogQL — counts: gpu-agent ~12.1k missing, kvcache-uploader ~3.2k, model-fanout ~820. sample: `2026-02-04T02:06:18Z level=warn msg="failed write, retrying" trace_id="" pod=gpu-agent-12 node=gpu-node-12 err="write reset"`
sre-oncall: created a temp Grafana dashboard correlating `rate(loki_ingester_write_errors[1m])` vs `increase(missing_trace_id_total[10m])` and set a provisional alert when missing_trace_id_ratio > 0.1% sustained for 30m
marta: devtask: preserve trace header across retry paths in the log agent serializer (PR opened: https://git/internal/pull/9876). ETA ~6 hours for review/merge. short-term: increase agent in-memory retry buffer and enable raw payload logging for failed batches.
jasper: added Loki pipeline stage to set label `trace_id_missing=true` for records with empty trace_id to make downstream evals/filtering simpler. also trying to rehydrate from `http_headers.x-trace-id` if present.
sre-oncall: conntrack drops dropped after bump; Loki query p95 trending back toward ~420-500ms over 20m. keeping incident open until missing_trace_id ratio < 0.1% for 30m.
emma: action items: 1) keep NAT rollback until maintenance window, 2) finish kube-proxy arg rollout + conntrack bump across gpu pool, 3) land serializer fix and deploy, 4) keep Grafana alert and incident until stable.
net-eng: we'll follow up with a postmortem focused on NAT rotation gating and staging soak; also check cloud provider's NAT session TTL settings. :eyes:
marta: updating INC-3421 with timeline, LogQL/Kibana queries, dashboards and PR links; tagging compliance for audit log retention verification.
emma: thanks — updates here please. :thumbsup:
